notes: Future Land Use (FLU) categories treated as multifamily-supportive or higher-density. GIS codes come from Orange County Open Data layer 21 (unincorporated + annexed parcels still on county FLU) and Orlando Open Data layer 83. Municipal FLU besides Orlando is not in these public layers; those parcels stay unknown unless a city GIS feed is added. This file is the matching source of truth — edit here, not in the app.

sources.label: Orange County Future Land Use GIS
Orange County Future Land Use and Zoning Correlation (Jan 2021)
Orange County Planning and Zoning Quick Reference Guide
City of Orlando Future Land Use legend

categories.label: Low-Medium Density Residential (LMDR)
categories.why: County correlation table: LMDR up to 10 du/ac + workforce housing bonus. Can support townhouse / small multifamily; not high-rise.

categories.label: Medium Density Residential (MDR)
categories.why: County correlation: MDR 20 du/ac + workforce housing bonus; consistent zoning includes R-2, R-3, UR-3, PD, U-V. GIS code MD.

categories.label: Medium-High Density Residential
categories.why: Comprehensive Plan / correlation table: MHDR 35 du/ac + workforce housing bonus; consistent zoning R-2, R-3, UR-3, PD, U-V. Present as a GIS LAND_USE value even though some layer legends only draw MD and HD.

categories.label: High Density Residential (HDR)
categories.why: County correlation: HDR 50 du/ac + workforce housing bonus; consistent zoning R-2, R-3, UR-3, PD, U-V. GIS code HD.

categories.label: Neighborhood Residential
categories.why: County correlation: NR 20 du/ac / 0.4 FAR; paired with NR zoning. Intended for neighborhood-scale housing including attached product.

categories.label: Neighborhood Activity Corridor
categories.why: County correlation: NAC 25 du/ac / 1.0 FAR. Mixed corridor that includes residential density.

categories.label: Neighborhood Center
categories.why: County correlation: NC 40 du/ac / 2.0 FAR. Mixed neighborhood-center designation.

categories.label: Activity Center Residential (I-Drive)
categories.why: I-Drive Activity Center Residential. Densities follow the I-Drive Element / Strategic Development Plan rather than the standard MDR/HDR table; typically PD-implemented.

categories.label: Activity Center Mixed Use (I-Drive)
categories.why: I-Drive Activity Center Mixed Use. Residential is contemplated; confirm the I-Drive Element and any PD for site density.

categories.label: Traditional Neighborhood (Avalon Park)
categories.why: TND is the Avalon Park traditional neighborhood designation, implemented through PD. Includes mixed housing types; site density is plan-specific.

categories.label: Community Village Center
categories.why: Four Corners CVC; county notes new CVC requests closed after Sept 2009. Mixed village-center; entitlements are existing-plan specific.

categories.label: Village (Horizon West)
categories.why: Horizon West Village FLU. Densities and housing mix are in the adopted village land-use plan / PD, not a countywide du/ac cap. Treat as site-specific.

categories.label: Planned Development (FLU)
categories.why: PD on the FLUM is not a density entitlement by itself. Policies FLU8.1.2 / FLU8.1.4 and the PD ordinance control. Maybe — site-specific.

categories.label: Low Density Residential (LDR)
categories.why: LDR 4 du/ac. Correlation is single-family districts (R-1 series, R-CE, R-T-1/2, R-L-D). Not treated as multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Rural / Agricultural
categories.why: Rural/agricultural FLU. Not multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Rural Settlement 1/1
categories.why: Rural Settlement 1 du/ac. Not multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Rural Settlement 1/2
categories.why: Rural Settlement 1 du / 2 ac. Not multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Rural Settlement 1/5
categories.why: Rural Settlement 1 du / 5 ac. Not multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Rural Settlement Low Density
categories.why: Rural Settlement Low Density (about 2 du/ac per the county quick-reference guide). Not treated as multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Office
categories.why: County Office FLU correlates with office zoning, not residential density. Live Local Act reviews are a zoning-path issue, not this FLU category.

categories.label: Commercial
categories.why: County Commercial FLU is not a residential designation. Do not treat commercial FLUM as a rezoning-to-apartments green light.

categories.label: Industrial
categories.why: Industrial FLU. Not treated as multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Institutional
categories.why: Institutional FLU.

categories.label: Education
categories.why: Education FLU.

categories.label: Parks / Recreation
categories.why: Parks and recreation / open space.

categories.label: Preservation
categories.why: Preservation.

categories.label: Water Body
categories.why: Water body.

categories.label: Innovation Way
categories.why: Innovation Way overlay on the county FLUM. Mixed-use and employment-center policies apply; residential density is plan/PD specific. Maybe — do not treat as by-right MDR.

categories.label: Lake Pickett
categories.why: Lake Pickett overlay. Not treated as a countywide multifamily FLU. Confirm the Lake Pickett adopted policies before assuming apartments.

categories.label: Municipal (county layer placeholder)
categories.why: County GIS code for land inside a city. Not a FLU category. The join script prefers Orlando layer 83 when that point hits; other cities remain unknown.

categories.label: Residential, Medium Intensity
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Residential Medium Intensity min 12 / max 30 du/ac. Multifamily-supportive.

categories.label: Residential, High Intensity
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Residential High Intensity min 30 / max 200 du/ac.

categories.label: Residential Medium / Resource Protection
categories.why: Same medium-intensity residential FLU with a resource-protection overlay. Overlay may limit the buildable envelope; density category still contemplates MF.

categories.label: Residential High / Resource Protection
categories.why: High-intensity residential FLU with resource-protection overlay.

categories.label: Mixed Use Corridor, Medium Intensity
categories.why: Orlando GMP: MUC-Medium min 15 / max 30 du/ac. Mixed-use corridor including residential.

categories.label: Mixed Use Corridor, High Intensity
categories.why: Orlando GMP: MUC-High min 30 / max 200 du/ac.

categories.label: Mixed Use Corridor Medium / Resource Protection
categories.why: MUC-Medium with resource-protection overlay.

categories.label: Mixed Use / Neighborhood Development
categories.why: Orlando GMP: MU-ND max 12 du/ac. Mixed neighborhood; can include small attached product but is not a high-density MF designation.

categories.label: Mixed Use / Neighborhood Development / Resource Protection
categories.why: MU-ND with resource-protection overlay; max still 12 du/ac.

categories.label: Neighborhood Activity Center
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Neighborhood Activity Center min 15 / max 30 du/ac. Activity centers are mixed-use including residential. Implemented in part by AC-N zoning.

categories.label: Community Activity Center
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Community Activity Center min 20 / max 40 du/ac. AC-1 zoning implements this category.

categories.label: Urban Activity Center
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Urban Activity Center min 30 / max 100 du/ac. AC-2 zoning.

categories.label: Metropolitan Activity Center
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Metropolitan Activity Center min 30 / max 200 du/ac. AC-3 / AC-3A zoning.

categories.label: Downtown Activity Center
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Downtown Activity Center min 75 / max 200 du/ac / 4.0 FAR.

categories.label: Urban Village
categories.why: Urban Village FLU supports mixed residential. Confirm the village regulating plan for density.

categories.label: Office, Medium Intensity
categories.why: Orlando FLU legend lists Office Medium max 40 du/ac (min 12). Residential is contemplated alongside office; still confirm zoning (O-2 / multiplex rules in Ch. 58 Part 3H).

categories.label: Office, High Intensity
categories.why: Orlando FLU legend lists Office High max 200 du/ac (min 30). Residential density is on the FLUM; zoning must still allow the product.

categories.label: Office, Low Intensity
categories.why: Office Low is not listed with a residential density band in the public legend used for this pass. Not treated as MF-supportive by default.

categories.label: Residential, Low Intensity
categories.why: Orlando GMP: Residential Low max 12 du/ac, no minimum. Typically single-family / low-intensity neighborhoods. Not treated as multifamily-supportive FLU.

categories.label: Residential Low / Resource Protection
categories.why: Low-intensity residential with resource-protection overlay.

categories.label: Industrial
categories.why: Industrial FLU. Not treated as MF-supportive without a site-specific policy. Do not assume Live Local from FLU alone.

categories.label: Conservation
categories.why: Conservation.

categories.label: Public / Recreational and Institutional
categories.why: Public, recreational, and institutional.

categories.label: Airport Support District, High Intensity
categories.why: Airport support. Not treated as residential FLU.

categories.label: Airport Support District, Medium Intensity
categories.why: Airport support. Not treated as residential FLU.
